correctness.rationale: Source equations (2.3)–(2.4) specialize algebraically to the iid one-delay-step companion. Exact integration builds the six-coordinate moment operator, whose determinant is s Q(s)/12. Sturm variations at 0 and 3/2 are 4 and 3, proving a unique relevant root. The cone-preserving moment map has a positive-definite adjoint Perron eigenmatrix because the companions have no common proper invariant subspace, giving the exact growth rate for every nonzero deterministic state. Perturbation at zero and the determinant sign establish the stable/unstable intervals below sqrt(2); above sqrt(2), the deterministic mean companion determinant and Jensen exclude stability. Exact Routh–Hurwitz coefficients at s=7/6 establish mean stability, while det(I-M)<0 proves mean-square growth. The variance decomposition gives monotone moment spectral radius. Standalone SymPy verification completed 24 checks.

originality.rationale: The source 2024 algorithm is an actual delayed-stage randomized RK method but supplies fixed-horizon convergence, not an exact infinite-horizon mean-square stability threshold. A prior randomized ODE scalar test yields a different one-multiplier stability criterion, and deterministic DDE methods likewise do not determine the random companion covariance. The degree-seven threshold with exact one-crossing proof, all-positive-parameter boundary, and rational mean/mean-square reversal are new to the literature inspected and distinct from previously available scientific findings. Residual risks include undiscovered stochastic recurrence equivalences; originality is a self-review, not a claim of exhaustive priority.

value.rationale: Infinite-horizon moment stability is a natural practical question for an iid-stage method with finite-horizon error analysis. An exact sharp threshold and exact stable-mean/unstable-second-moment witness at a simple rational step clarify the reliability limits of randomized delay integration, and the variance-order law identifies the structural cause. This is a motivated full parameter classification for the smallest nontrivial delay grid, not an arbitrary computed number. Its relevance is limited to the specified scalar test family, which is stated explicitly.
